chapter: Looking back and the lean years
title: Hating territory-band mute effects and not caring about money
summary: He could not stand jerky wah-wah arrangements, tolerated theater bands because he was featured, and says happiness mattered more than pay.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: You never did stick with that kind of stuff---
Oh, I couldn't take it - I just couldn't take it. Of course, I could stand the big theater orchestra because I got featured occasionally- blow and play ---

I think that - my own opinion is that - you're--- to you, the way you play is your form of self-expression rather than a job - like going to the bank everyday, which it is with a lot of musicians; they'll play anything they can do to earn their money.
Well, it's a funny thing - I never considered money in this thing. Only if I was unhappy. If I was unhappy, it wouldn't make any difference how much money I was making.

I would have quit anyway. But, if I was with a band that was really rocking and really going, I'd love it no matter what they paid me-- you know, so money was never a big thing in my--- (end of Tape 3 - Side Two)---
